difficultyRationale: Platform-estimated: two directly linked concepts (deducing opposite faces from three dice views, then reading opposite faces off a cube net) in 2-3 steps, with an optional mirror-image check; about 2-3 min.
stem:
Three different views of a dice are shown in the figure below.

![Figure: three views of the same die. View 1: 5 on top, 4 on the front-left face, 1 on the front-right face. View 2: 4 on top, 6 front-left, 3 front-right. View 3: 2 on top, 6 front-left, 5 front-right.](/pyq/2024/fig/Q09-1.png)

The piece of paper that can be folded to make this dice is

options.label: A
options.text: ![Figure: net A. Top row: 5, 1. Below 1, a vertical column: 4, 6, 2. To the right of 2: 3.](/pyq/2024/fig/Q09-2.png)

options.label: B
options.text: ![Figure: net B. Top row: 5, 1. Below 1, a vertical column: 4, 2, 6. To the right of 6: 3.](/pyq/2024/fig/Q09-3.png)

options.label: C
options.text: ![Figure: net C. Top row: 5, 1. Below 1, a vertical column: 3, 2, 4. To the right of 4: 6.](/pyq/2024/fig/Q09-4.png)

options.label: D
options.text: ![Figure: net D. Top row: 5, 1. Below 1, a vertical column: 4, 6, 3. To the right of 3: 2.](/pyq/2024/fig/Q09-5.png)

solution.quick: From the views, 4 touches 5, 1, 6, 3, so 4 is opposite 2; 6 touches 4, 3, 2, 5, so 6 is opposite 1; hence 3 is opposite 5. In each net, alternate squares of the vertical strip are opposite and the two side flaps are opposite. Only net (A) gives the pairs 1–6, 4–2, 5–3, and its corner 5 → 1 → 4 runs clockwise, as in view 1. Answer: **(A)**.

steps.title: Record which faces are seen together
steps.body:
Faces visible in the same view share an edge (they are adjacent), so they cannot be opposite.

| View | Top | Front-left | Front-right |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 5 | 4 | 1 |
| 2 | 4 | 6 | 3 |
| 3 | 2 | 6 | 5 |

steps.title: Deduce the three opposite pairs
steps.body:
- **Face 4** is seen with 5 and 1 (view 1) and with 6 and 3 (view 2). That is four distinct neighbours, so the only remaining face, **2, is opposite 4**.
- **Face 6** is seen with 4 and 3 (view 2) and with 2 and 5 (view 3). That is four distinct neighbours, so **1 is opposite 6**.
- The remaining two faces give the last pair: **3 is opposite 5**.

Required pairs: $\{1,6\},\ \{2,4\},\ \{3,5\}$.

steps.title: Read the opposite pairs from each net
steps.body:
All four nets have the same shape: a vertical strip of four squares, one square attached to the **left** of the top square, and one attached to the **right** of the bottom square. When folded, the strip wraps around the cube like a belt, so the 1st and 3rd squares are opposite, and so are the 2nd and 4th. The two side flaps close the two ends of the belt, so they are opposite each other.

| Net | Strip (top → bottom) | Flaps | Opposite pairs | Conflict with views |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 1, 4, 6, 2 | 5, 3 | 1–6, 4–2, 5–3 | none |
| B | 1, 4, 2, 6 | 5, 3 | 1–2, 4–6, 5–3 | 4 and 6 are adjacent (view 2) |
| C | 1, 3, 2, 4 | 5, 6 | 1–2, 3–4, 5–6 | 3 and 4 are adjacent (view 2); 5 and 6 are adjacent (view 3) |
| D | 1, 4, 6, 3 | 5, 2 | 1–6, 4–3, 5–2 | 4 and 3 are adjacent (view 2); 2 and 5 are adjacent (view 3) |

Only net (A) has the required opposite pairs.

steps.title: Rule out a mirror image for net (A)
steps.body:
The same opposite pairs can occur on two mirror-image dice, so check one corner's orientation. With the printed side becoming the outside of the cube, faces meet around a corner in the same cyclic order as they appear around the matching point of the flat net.

- **Net (A):** faces 5, 1 and 4 meet at the lower-left corner of square 1. Going clockwise around that point: 5 (upper-left) → 1 (upper-right) → 4 (lower-right). When folded, the free edges of 5 and 4 join.
- **View 1:** going clockwise around the visible corner: top 5 → front-right 1 → front-left 4.

The orders agree, so net (A) produces this die and not its mirror image. The opposite pairs plus one corner orientation fix a die completely. A full 3-D folding check (the Python in the verification) confirms that net (A) also reproduces views 2 and 3.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.body: Net (A) is the only piece of paper that folds into the die shown. The answer is **(A)**.

solution.teaching:
**Faces of a cube.** A cube has 6 faces forming 3 opposite pairs. Each face touches (shares an edge with) the other four faces, every face except its opposite. Two consequences are useful for dice questions:

1. Faces seen together in one view are adjacent, never opposite.
2. If a face is seen, across several views, next to four different faces, the one face never seen with it is its opposite.

**Nets (unfolded cubes).** A net is the paper that folds into the cube. Squares sharing an edge in the net share an edge on the cube. In a straight strip, alternate squares (1st and 3rd, 2nd and 4th) become opposite, because the strip wraps around the cube. A strip of four forms a closed "belt" of four side faces, and the squares attached on either side of the belt become the two remaining faces, the lid and the base, so they are opposite each other. Squares that do *not* touch in the flat net are not necessarily opposite: here, 5 and 4 do not touch in net (A) but are adjacent on the cube.

**Mirror images.** Opposite pairs do not fully determine a die. A die and its mirror image have the same opposite pairs, but the faces around each corner run in opposite directions (clockwise versus anticlockwise). To distinguish them, compare the cyclic order around one corner in a view with the order around the matching point of the net, looking at the printed side, which becomes the outside of the cube.

**This question.** The views give 4–2 and 6–1 directly (4 and 6 each appear in two views with four different neighbours), leaving 3–5. The belt-and-flaps rule reads the opposite pairs off each net in seconds, and only (A) matches. A clockwise check of the 5 → 1 → 4 corner confirms that (A) is not a mirror image.

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.explanation: Strip 1, 4, 6, 2 gives 1–6 and 4–2 as opposite pairs, and flaps 5 and 3 are opposite: exactly the pairs required by the views. The corner 5 → 1 → 4 runs clockwise in the net, as in view 1, so this is not the mirror-image die.

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.explanation: Strip 1, 4, 2, 6 makes 4 opposite 6 and 1 opposite 2, but view 2 shows 4 and 6 side by side, and 1 must be opposite 6.

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.explanation: Strip 1, 3, 2, 4 makes 3 opposite 4 (adjacent in view 2), and flaps 5 and 6 opposite (adjacent in view 3).

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.explanation: Strip 1, 4, 6, 3 makes 4 opposite 3 (adjacent in view 2), and flaps 5 and 2 opposite (adjacent in view 3). The pair 1–6 is right, but the other two pairs are wrong.

solution.shortcut: Find the opposite of each number that appears in two views (here 4 → 2 and 6 → 1, which leaves 3–5). Then read each net's opposite pairs with the rule "alternate squares in a straight strip are opposite". This eliminates B, C and D immediately.
solution.commonTrap: Assuming that squares which do not touch in the flat net must be opposite (e.g. 5 and 4 in net A are actually adjacent), or matching only the opposite pairs without noticing that a mirror-image arrangement would also have them. Here the opposite pairs alone already single out (A).

answerVerification.method: Author solve (not blind) compared with official key
answerVerification.notes: The opposite pairs deduced from the views, {1,6}, {2,4} and {3,5}, match only net A. A 3-D folding simulation with a corner-orientation (determinant) check confirms that net A reproduces all three views with the correct handedness, and that B, C and D fail. This matches the official key A.
